The diagram demonstrates a high level of organization and readability for a microservices architecture. It successfully uses visual hierarchy to separate concerns: incoming traffic (Front services), core business logic (GeoServer), supporting infrastructure, and persistence layers. The flow is logically oriented from top to bottom (Request -> Processing -> Storage), making it easy to trace the life of a request. The use of group-level connectors (e.g., the line from the "GeoServer" box to the "Event Bus") is an excellent design choice that prevents the "spaghetti code" effect often seen in microservice diagrams, keeping the visual noise low while accurately conveying that all contained services share that connection. Additionally, the notation [0..N] clearly communicates scalability without needing extra text.
